messages:
Alex L: quick thread — thoughts on routing + quota isolation when mixing hosted / dedicated / private?
Alex L: specifically: if hosted is overloaded and we fallback to dedicated, how do we avoid dedicated customers getting hammered (or billed) unexpectedly?
Maria G: we should treat fallback as explicit opt-in per-tenant. idea: capacity tokens + fallback flag. fallback_consumed is billed to the caller app, not the dedicated reservation.
Samir K: +1 to opt-in. also, cross-env fallback to private has latency and security implications — we should default private->no-fallback.
Jen T: observability req: every request needs env_origin, route_decision, and billing_bucket tags so we can trace cost/latency back to a decision.
Alex L: agreed on private default off. what about reserved dedicated pools — can they choose to allow "best-effort borrow" during quiet times?
Maria G: yes — three modes: strict (no borrow), reserve (keep baseline, allow small burst), borrow (allow larger bursts billed differently). we need router policy semantics for this.
Samir K: latency tradeoff: borrow implies routing across cloud region or shared network. for strict SLOs, borrow should be disabled. we should document network RTT assumptions in the policy.
Jen T: quick example config snippet (proposal):
```
router_policy:
  allowed_destinations: [HOSTED, DEDICATED]
  quota_mode: reserve   # strict | reserve | borrow
  fallback_rules:
    - when: cpu>80% OR backlog>200
      to: DEDICATED
      billing: caller
      allowed_models: [gpt-medium, gpt-small-fallback]
```
Maria G: that DSL is fine. implementation note: keep decision synchronous and cheap — no distributed consensus per request. evaluate policy in the control plane and cache decisions locally in edge routers.
Alex L: what about abuse vectors? tenant A could intentionally cause a spike to trigger borrow and spike cost for tenant B if billing isn't separated.
Maria G: mitigation: enforce per-tenant burst caps and require billing authorization for cross-tenant borrow. dedicated pool owner can set an alert/auto-reject threshold.
Samir K: also add a circuit-breaker: if borrow rate exceeds X% of pool for Y mins then reject all further borrows and notify owners.
ops-bot: RFC reference: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1967-hybrid-routing (updated)
Alex L: next actions: 1) Spike to validate latency for private->dedicated fallbacks (Samir + EngInfra), 2) Add router_policy DSL draft to RFC (Maria), 3) Console UX proposal to toggle fallback/borrow per-tenant (Jen).
Jen T: noted, I'll prototype toggles and telemetry columns. :thumbsup:
Alex L: scheduling 30m sync Friday to decide defaults. thanks all.
